prompt: The Star Wars kinrath in its netcaster design (owner-ruled), side view, head facing RIGHT, following the attached canon closely: it is shaped most like a praying mantis crossed with a long-legged spider. GEOMETRY (from the donor sprite, follow exactly): a compact, thick, upright segmented thorax-neck column, tilted slightly forward, rising from a low rounded rear abdomen; directly on top a short, blunt, box-shaped head about as wide as the column (no long S-curved snake neck, no sleek snake head); the head is roughly 15% of the animal's height, the torso column roughly 45%. SIX limbs: two raptorial mantis forelimbs on the upper thorax, the upper arm angled forward and up, the forearm folded down and back into a hooked, spined mantis claw (the near one in front of the chest, the far one just visible behind it); and four long, thin, multi-jointed walking legs hinged at the lower thorax, two splayed to the rear and two to the front, each with a long upper segment angled UP to a high knee well above the body line, then a long lower segment angled DOWN to a pointed dark-tipped foot: a wide, low, spider-like crouch with the body slung between the knees, the leg span almost the full canvas width. FACE (canon netcaster): six round glossy black eyes in a tight cluster on the front of the blunt head, small mandibles below, and beneath them a small six-petaled orange-red flower organ. BODY: spoon-shaped, narrow at the top and wider toward the rear, the abdomen crossed by dark brown horizontal bands. COLOUR (canon): warm yellow-gold to tan-brown chitin, rust-orange patches at the joints, darker brown abdomen bands; no blue anywhere. Render it as a real arthropod: glossy segmented chitin with natural wear and fine texture, natural light, real anatomy, not the animation's flat shading. Whole animal inside the canvas with margin. No ground, no shadow, no outline. LEG COUNT IS EXACT: count the walking legs before finishing. Exactly FOUR walking legs in total (not five, not six) and no leg or foot descending beneath the belly or the middle of the body; the two raptorial claws are arms, not walking legs, and are separate from the four.
